name: claudestream
help: Drive Claude Code from the command line: start a session under a claudewheel profile, send one prompt, and print the reply as final text, live text, a detailed rendering, or the raw stream-json lines; run agent definitions; and check the installation

ask.name: ask
ask.help: Send one prompt to Claude Code and print only the reply's final text on stdout; with --json, the reply and its metadata are the document's payload. A turn that Claude Code ends with an error exits 1 with the result text on stderr
ask.dry_run_unsupported_reason: Claude Code runs as a subprocess whose file edits, commands, and API spend happen outside the effects handle, so a dry run could record none of them

flags.name: model
flags.help: Claude model for the session, passed to Claude Code as --model (an alias such as sonnet or opus, or a full model ID)

flags.name: profile
flags.help: claudewheel profile the session runs under: Claude Code is started as `claudewheel profile exec --name <profile> -- <claude> ...`, which gives it the profile's environment

flags.name: prompt-source
flags.help: Where the prompt comes from: pass --prompt or --prompt-from-stdin

choices.name: prompt
choices.help: send this flag's value as the prompt

flags.name: value
flags.help: Prompt text to send

choices.name: prompt-from-stdin
choices.help: read the prompt from standard input

flags.name: session
flags.help: Which Claude Code session to use: pass --new-session, --resume, or --continue-session

choices.name: new-session
choices.help: start a new session

choices.name: resume
choices.help: resume the session with this ID

flags.name: value
flags.help: ID of the session to resume

choices.name: continue-session
choices.help: continue the most recent session in the working directory

flags.name: skip-permissions
flags.help: Required either way: --skip-permissions runs Claude Code with --dangerously-skip-permissions, so no tool use is checked; --no-skip-permissions keeps Claude Code's permission checks, so tools that need permission are refused

flags.name: cwd
flags.help: Working directory for Claude Code; when omitted, Claude Code runs in this process's working directory

flags.name: system-prompt
flags.help: System prompt for the session, passed to Claude Code as --system-prompt; when omitted, Claude Code uses its own

flags.name: from-pr
flags.help: GitHub pull request to load into the session, passed to Claude Code as --from-pr; when omitted, none is loaded

flags.name: claude-binary
flags.help: Absolute path of the Claude Code executable; when omitted, `claude` is looked up on PATH

flags.name: claudewheel-binary
flags.help: Absolute path of the claudewheel executable; when omitted, `claudewheel` is looked up on PATH

flags.name: color
flags.help: --color colors the output and --no-color does not; when neither is passed, stdout and stderr are each colored only when they are a terminal and NO_COLOR is unset or empty

flags.name: footer
flags.help: --footer writes a line with the turn's duration and cost to stderr after the reply and --no-footer does not; when neither is passed, the line is written (events with --json never writes it: its stderr carries the --json document)

stream.name: stream
stream.help: Send one prompt to Claude Code and write the reply's text to stdout as it arrives, with a one-line marker on stderr for each thinking block, tool call, tool result, and notice. A turn that Claude Code ends with an error exits 1 with the result text on stderr
stream.dry_run_unsupported_reason: Claude Code runs as a subprocess whose file edits, commands, and API spend happen outside the effects handle, so a dry run could record none of them

doctor.name: doctor
doctor.help: Check what a session needs: the claude path and its version against the minimum 2.0.0 (`claude -v`, within 2s), and the claudewheel path; with --profile, also run `claudewheel profile exec --name <profile> -- <claude> -v` (within 10s). Prints one [ok] or [FAIL] line per check and exits 1 when any check fails

flags.name: profile
flags.help: claudewheel profile to check by starting Claude Code under it; when omitted, no profile is checked

flags.name: claude-binary
flags.help: Absolute path of the Claude Code executable to check; when omitted, `claude` is looked up on PATH

flags.name: claudewheel-binary
flags.help: Absolute path of the claudewheel executable to check; when omitted, `claudewheel` is looked up on PATH

agent.name: agent
agent.help: Run and inspect agent definitions: strict TOML files at .claudestream/agents/<name>.agent.toml (format_version = 2) that declare a prompt template with {variable} placeholders and, optionally, a model, tools, a sandbox, budget thresholds, MCP servers, and stream options

run.name: run
run.help: Run one prompt through an agent definition and write the reply's text to stdout as it arrives, with markers on stderr as the stream command writes them. The agent's resolved prompt template becomes the system prompt, its name the session name, and its sandbox, budget, MCP, and stream tables replace the defaults. With --agent-name, the agents directory is searched under --cwd, or under the current directory when --cwd is omitted. Agents that declare tools are refused: their handlers exist only in Go programs that call the agent package. A turn that Claude Code ends with an error exits 1 with the result text on stderr
run.dry_run_unsupported_reason: Claude Code runs as a subprocess whose file edits, commands, and API spend happen outside the effects handle, so a dry run could record none of them
